issues.legal_issue: A suit against the government or a public officer for which prior notice is required cannot be instituted before the statutory waiting period after delivery of notice has expired.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought a declaration of title and delivery of possession of immovable property, with mesne profits, against the State as the main defendant.
The plaintiffs delivered written notice to the State before bringing the suit but instituted the suit before the required two-month period had expired.
The trial court dismissed the suit as not maintainable for want of proper notice, and the appellate courts upheld that result.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not maintainable because it was instituted before the required two-month period had expired; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as it stood before its amendment by Act 104 of 1976, imposes a mandatory bar on instituting a covered suit until two months after notice is delivered in the prescribed manner. The provision serves the public purpose of giving the government or officer an opportunity to examine and settle a claim, avoiding unnecessary litigation and expense. Clear and unambiguous statutory language must be given effect despite hardship, and the requirement admits no implied exception for urgent relief. The Court relied on Bhagchand Dagadusa v. Secretary of State for India, Vellayan v. Madras Province, and Sawai Singhai Nirmal Chand v. Union of India, and rejected Nani Amma Nannini Amma v. State of Kerala as no longer good law. The Court also stated that the position remained unaltered for a suit of this nature under the amended provision.

predicates.notice_requirement_applies: The proceeding is a suit against the government or a public officer for which prior written notice is required.
predicates.notice_delivered: The plaintiff delivered written notice to the government or officer before instituting the suit.
predicates.suit_filed_before_waiting_period_expired: The plaintiff instituted the suit before the required period following delivery of notice had expired.
predicates.suit_is_not_maintainable_and_must_be_dis: The suit cannot be maintained and must be dismissed.

issues.definition: When a covered suit is brought after notice has been delivered but before the required waiting period has expired, the suit cannot be maintained and must be dismissed.
